key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings form dense, fine-lamellar microstructures when droplet spreading is optimized, improving long-term corrosion and humidity-dependent wear performance.
engineering_relevance: This work supports using process-controlled amorphous coatings on carbon steel to extend service life in corrosive and variable-humidity environments.
method: Deposited Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spray parameters.
Evaluated coating microstructure, porosity, corrosion resistance, and tribological behavior.
Tested wear under different humidity conditions with Si3N4 counterbodies to assess tribo-chemical effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coatings with disk-like droplets, higher circularity/expansion, and lower porosity showed better corrosion resistance, while friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance appears sensitive to porosity and ambient humidity, so process control and operating-environment consistency are critical for reliable deployment.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
